trust_decision.summary: Whether the user-writable saved_search.contents field may be deserialised with PHP classes allowed; decided separately at each reader (FilterContentMapper, FilterDefinitionProvider) and, after the fix, also at the write chokepoint SavedSearch::save, which re-encodes contents as JSON.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'SavedSearch Filter Processing'; this is the SavedSearch filter mapper, and it calls unserialize with allowed_classes => true explicitly.

fix_sites.entry_point: Suite 8 API read of a SavedSearch record or list (ApiBeanMapper::toApi -> toApi -> parseContent); mapper registered at public/legacy/include/portability/ApiBeanMapper/ModuleMappers/SavedSearch/SavedSearchMappers.php:41
Suite 8 API save of an existing SavedSearch (ApiBeanMapper::toBean -> FilterContentMapper::toBean decodes the stored contents before merging)
Same save path; encode() changes the write format from base64+serialize to JSON

Suite 8 list-view metadata (ListViewDefinitionHandler availableFilters, core/backend/ViewDefinitions/LegacyHandler/ListViewDefinitionHandler.php:260); here unserialize is called with no options, so all classes are allowed
fix_sites.module_kind: Symfony core service (second implementation of the contents decoder)

fix_sites.entry_point: Any bean save of SavedSearch, including legacy V8 JSON:API create/update (public/legacy/Api/V8/Service/ModuleService.php:276, :441), which assign raw attributes at :478
fix_sites.module_kind: legacy bean (write-side sanitiser at the save chokepoint)

fix_sites.entry_point: Legacy list views with saved_search_select (public/legacy/include/MVC/View/views/view.list.php:175); already allowed_classes=false, changed only for the JSON format
Legacy saved-search select/redirect flow; already allowed_classes=false, format only
Legacy saved-search save from $_REQUEST (handleSave); write format changed to JSON
Admin upgrade routine; already allowed_classes=false, format only
Doctrine migration run on upgrade (bin/console migrations); converts stored rows to JSON

O3_reason_to_dismiss: FilterDefinitionProvider is a separate Symfony-core metadata service in another package. It only reads the current user's own saved searches (core/backend/Filters/Service/FilterDefinitionProvider.php:70-75) to build list-view 'availableFilters', so a solver can argue that it is not 'SavedSearch filter processing' and that the data is the user's own.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing saved filters stored as base64(serialize(array)) must still load, and legitimate nested arrays (multi-select values from $_REQUEST) must round-trip. If a fix drops the legacy decode, or the save path rejects or purifies non-object contents (purify_html in cleanBean would mangle JSON), users' saved filters break.

O6_input_shapes: base64(serialize(array)) legacy format (must still decode, classes disallowed)

O7_producer.where: public/legacy/include/portability/ApiBeanMapper/ModuleMappers/SavedSearch/FilterContentMapper.php:181-188 (encode) and public/legacy/modules/SavedSearch/SavedSearch.php:423 (handleSave); a raw writer that bypasses both is public/legacy/Api/V8/Service/ModuleService.php:478

O8b_injection_room.sibling: user_preferences.contents decoded as base64(serialize) for the V8 API; a sibling would decode it with classes allowed (as FilterContentMapper does), in a separate API package
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same storage idiom (base64+serialize contents column) and the same 'contents' naming. A maintainer copying the FilterContentMapper style into a V8 preferences service would plausibly write allowed_classes => true.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second core service (for example a saved-filter export or default-filter provider) in core/backend that reads saved_search.contents with plain unserialize()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pinned core service already does exactly this with no options, so a second Symfony-side reader written the same way is consistent with the codebase.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a helper beside sugar_unserialize that skips the object regex/allowed_classes for 'trusted' DB fields
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Legacy code mixes sugar_unserialize and raw unserialize; a 'fast path' variant for internal fields is a plausible maintainer shortcut.

O9_family: CWE-502 unsafe deserialisation of a user-writable stored field (save/reload boundary)

O10_build.language: PHP (Symfony 6 core + legacy SuiteCRM 7 tree), Angular frontend
O10_build.toolchain: PHP 8.x with composer (core and public/legacy); yarn/Angular only needed for UI
services: web server (Apache/nginx + php-fpm) for HTTP-level tests
O10_build.project_tests: Core PHPUnit tests under tests/ (none cover FilterContentMapper or SavedSearch); legacy public/legacy/tests/unit/phpunit/modules/SavedSearch/SavedSearchTest.php

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change allowed_classes => true to false at the two FilterContentMapper calls only, leaving the bare unserialize in core FilterDefinitionProvider and adding no write-side check in SavedSearch::save.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit is the 8.9.3 release commit. It bundles unrelated ACLAccess('view'/'edit') checks (LinkedRecordsProvider, Subpanel/HistoryTimeline/ProspectList handlers, RecordHandler, RecordMarkAsRead/Snooze) and User entity ApiProperty hardening. These are separate advisories, and they explain c_same_check_name=ACLAccess.
